description: Autonomous AI pentesting agents — real-time reconnaissance, vulnerability detection, and exploitation orchestration. Go + TypeScript.

written.description: Runs a second, independent agent whose only job is to re-exploit what the first one claimed, so a finding is either reproduced or dropped. One self-hosted binary with a local dashboard.

alive.last_commit_message:
feat(agent): inject into request bodies in verify_sqli/verify_ssti; widen SQL signatures (#864)

The SQLi and SSTI verifiers only ever placed their payload in the query
string, even for POST, so a parameter that lives in a JSON or form body
— the kind probe_body_contract discovers — could not be confirmed.

Add a shared injectionPoint helper (inject_in query|body, body_type
json|form, optional base_body for sibling fields) and route both
verifiers through it. Body injection defaults the method to POST, sets
the Content-Type, and merges the injected field into the supplied base
body so required siblings ride along and the request validates. The
query path is unchanged. Replaces the query-only sendInjectionProbe with
a body-capable sendInjectionRequest.

Also widen the shared DBMS error signatures with high-signal,
engine-specific PostgreSQL ("syntax error at or near", "unterminated
quoted string", "invalid input syntax for") and SQL Server ("incorrect
syntax near", "conversion failed when converting", OLE DB / ODBC driver
and SqlClient exception strings) tells, so error-based SQLi on those
engines is recognized. Each string is specific enough not to fire on a
benign page; LooksLikeSQLError and the reporting impact gate share the
one list.
